## What happened

At 01:52 the disk-usage alert for `db-3` fired. Priya Nair was on call. On arriving at her desk, the pager had already fired twice more. Wondering whether to fail over, the replica lag on the dashboard passed 40 minutes. Without a runbook for this alert, a restart seemed the fastest fix to her, and at 02:05 she ran `systemctl restart postgresql`. PostgreSQL came back at 02:07. Running on the same full volume as before. At 02:15 Priya paged Tomás Ruiz. The engineer who wrote the original WAL archiving script. A database engineer with ten years of PostgreSQL experience, the team had asked Tomás to own WAL archiving in 2024. At 02:31 he moved the WAL archive to `/mnt/archive`, and disk usage on `db-3` fell to 61%.

## Cause

`db-3` keeps its WAL archive on its data volume. The archive grows by about 9 GB a day. The cleanup job `wal-prune` deletes archive files that are older than three days. On 2026-09-28 a config change renamed the job's schedule key from `schedule` to `cron`, and `wal-prune` has not run since. The data volume of `db-3` filled up because `wal-prune` stopped running after that config change.

# The house on Mill Lane

We bought 14 Mill Lane in March. Being in terrible shape, we got the house for £40,000 under the asking price. Young and inexperienced, the rewiring seemed easy to me. It wasn't: it took me eleven weekends.

The sound of dripping water somewhere in the walls could be heard every night of the first week. There were a great number of dead leaves lying in the gutters, and the downpipe at the back had come loose. I found the original plans in the attic in April. Rolled up inside a 1962 newspaper.

The previous owner, Agnes, left notes everywhere. "Bleed radiators in October" is written on the boiler. Agnes' handwriting is also on the fuse box, inside the cupboards and on the back of the cellar door.

On our first night the cat vanished. I searched the cellar and the attic and called her name again and again. No reply. She turned up at breakfast, asleep in the airing cupboard.

I did not remember to cancel the old home insurance, so for six weeks we paid for two policies. And I still did not have much confidence in the surveyor's report, which called the roof "serviceable".

Edit this README section of `blobcache`, a caching proxy for object storage, for publication. Keep every fact, number, identifier and term. Output only the edited section.

## Cache behavior

`blobcache` uses the local disk for caching purposes only and never writes to the origin bucket. In the majority of cases, requests are served from the local disk. It has rarely been the case that a stale object was served after its origin copy was deleted, because the TTL of 300 seconds bounds that window. Errors of a transient nature, such as `503` from the origin, are retried; errors of a permanent character, such as `404`, are cached for 30 seconds.

Disk speed is the great factor in the cache's latency: the p99 is 4 ms on NVMe and 38 ms on network disks. Since v1.4, prefetching has become an increasingly important factor in reducing cold-start misses; it is behind the feature flag `prefetch.v2`. On a miss, `blobcache` fetches the object from the origin in a streaming manner, so the first bytes reach the client before the download ends.

Each entry is stored under the hash of its respective bucket and key. `blobcache` listens on ports 8080 and 9090 for the proxy and the metrics endpoint, respectively. The admin UI requires two-factor authentication.

Since v1.2 the project has used the code-owner system of review for this directory: the test cases in `evict_test.go` cover the edge case where the disk fills during a write, and every change to them needs a code owner's approval.

Edit this pull request description for `ledgerd` before I open the PR. Keep every fact, code span and opinion. Output only the edited description.

## Summary

Formerly, `ledgerd` was configured through environment variables, while now a YAML file at `/etc/ledgerd.yaml` is read. This PR changes the parser, the lexer, serializer and formatter. The new loader runs on Linux, macOS and on Windows. `ledgerd` never writes secrets from the YAML file to its logs.

## Why

The old loader did not pay any attention to `LEDGERD_DEBUG` after v1.4, and its startup benchmark was not honest: it measured a warm cache. The new loader starts 2 ms slower, which is not important for a daemon that runs for weeks.

I did not think that keeping both loaders was much use. My objections to keeping them are, first, the cost of maintaining two code paths; second, that environment variables would hide typos in key names.

## Upgrade notes

The migration was both a long job and very risky on our staging cluster: it took two days, and we rolled it back once. The new file lock is needed not for reads, but writes: reads already use snapshot isolation. Either you must pin `ledgerd` to v1.9 or convert your variables with `ledgerd config import`.

Write the runbook procedure "Replace a failed node" for the on-call engineers of the `prod-eu` Kubernetes cluster. Many of them read English as a second language. Use only the facts below, from the team's chat. Output only the procedure, starting with its heading.

Facts:
- First, log in to the cluster: `kubectl oidc-login --cluster prod-eu`. The team calls this "getting onto the cluster".
- Cordon the failed node, so that the scheduler places no new pods on it: `kubectl cordon <node>`.
- Drain the node: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`. Drain it only if the node is cordoned, the PodDisruptionBudget of every app on the node allows at least one more disruption (`kubectl get pdb -A` shows 1 or more under ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS), and no deploy is running in the cluster.
- Take the node out of the load balancer pool: `lbctl pool remove <node>`. The team says "take it out of the pool".
- Before you delete the node, make sure that no volume is still attached to it: `kubectl get volumeattachments | grep <node>` must print nothing. If you delete the node while a volume is attached, you lose the volume and its data. The local volumes have no backup.
- Delete the node: `kubectl delete node <node>`.
- If the replacement node does not join within 10 minutes, roll back the autoscaler config: `helm rollback node-autoscaler`.
- After the replacement node joins, test out the new node with the smoke-test chart: `helm install smoke ./charts/smoke-test --wait`.

## Why the runner stopped

The disk warnings for `ci-runner-7` went to `#ci-alerts-legacy`, a channel that nobody has watched since the March reorganization because the on-call rotation moved to PagerDuty, so the warnings went unread for nine days before the disk filled. Prior to 2026-09-28, the cache cleanup job `cache-prune` ran every night. On that day a config change renamed its schedule key from `schedule` to `cron`. `cache-prune` has not run since then. The build cache grew by in excess of 12 GB a day. The node disk pressure eviction threshold was 10%, so at 01:40 on 2026-10-07 the kubelet evicted the runner pods. The Grafana panel "Disk Pressure Eviction Count" showed the evictions. We raised the node disk pressure eviction threshold to 15% (`evictionHard: nodefs.available<15%`) and moved the warnings to `#ci-alerts`.
